s1.syndrome_frame: Postoperative spinal infection with neurological deficits
salient_findings: Cervical wound erythema with pus and saliva discharge
Lumbar spinal tenderness and bilateral leg weakness
Enterobacter cloacae cultured from the wound and blood
key_facts: Thoracoscopic esophagectomy with retrosternal gastric tube reconstruction and cervical esophagogastrostomy
Postoperative cervical wound erythema with pus and saliva discharge
Enterobacter cloacae cultured from the wound
Salvage reconstruction with a free jejunal autograft and pectoralis major muscle flap coverage
Worsening low back pain and fever (38.2 °C) 15 days after reconstruction
Lumbar spinal tenderness and bilateral leg weakness without sensory loss
MRI of the lumbar spine demonstrated decreased T1 signal and increased T2 and STIR signal at L4–L5

shortlist.label: Spondylodiscitis
shortlist.why_kept: Postoperative spinal infection with neurological deficits and Enterobacter cloacae bacteremia

shortlist.label: Epidural abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Lumbar spinal tenderness, bilateral leg weakness, and fever

shortlist.label: Spinal epidural abscess
shortlist.why_kept: MRI findings of decreased T1 signal and increased T2 and STIR signal at L4–L5

shortlist.label: Osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic infection and Enterobacter cloacae bacteremia

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of worsening low back pain and fever, along with the MRI findings of decreased T1 signal and increased T2 and STIR signal at L4-5, are consistent with spondylodiscitis, an infection of the intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebrae. The presence of Enterobacter cloacae in the blood cultures also supports this diagnosis, as it is a known cause of spondylodiscitis.

rejected.label: Epidural abscess
rejected.why: While the patient has symptoms of back pain and fever, the MRI findings do not specifically indicate an abscess in the epidural space.

rejected.label: Spinal epidural abscess
rejected.why: Similar to epidural abscess, the MRI findings do not specifically indicate an abscess in the spinal epidural space.

rejected.label: Discitis
rejected.why: While discitis is a possible diagnosis, spondylodiscitis is a more comprehensive diagnosis that includes infection of both the disc and adjacent vertebrae, which is consistent with the patient's symptoms and MRI findings.

rejected.label: Osteomyelitis
rejected.why: Osteomyelitis is a broader term that refers to infection of the bone, but spondylodiscitis is a more specific diagnosis that better explains the patient's symptoms and MRI findings.
